poc_plan_summary: POC goal is to validate Redwood Private in an AWS VPC with strict network controls. Success criteria (customer-stated): (1) private cluster can pull images without opening broad outbound internet, (2) logs/audit artifacts can be routed to customer-owned destinations (SIEM-friendly), (3) predictable networking pattern they can replicate for future environments, (4) document a path to on-prem later without re-architecting app-level integration. Redwood plan: use VPC Terraform modules (alpha) + installer preflight checks to harden endpoints/DNS/egress assumptions early.
target_architecture_notes: Target is AWS VPC, private subnets for worker nodes, no public node IPs. NAT is discouraged; customer prefers: VPC interface endpoints for ECR (api + dkr), STS, CloudWatch Logs (if used), SSM (optional), plus gateway endpoint for S3; remaining outbound via customer-managed egress proxy (explicit allowlist). Private DNS behavior for endpoints is a key decision point; customer wants deterministic DNS and minimal surprises. Ingress: internal load balancer only (no public ALB/NLB) for POC; connectivity from corp network via existing VPN today, DX later. On-prem requirement: keep dependency surface small; avoid SaaS control-plane coupling where possible; ask for packaging details once POC passes.
requirements_and_open_questions: IP planning: confirm RFC1918 ranges + any overlap with corp/on-prem networks (important for future DX).
DNS: do they use Route 53 Resolver inbound/outbound endpoints? any existing resolver rules to on-prem? who owns private hosted zones?
Egress: is a NAT gateway allowed at all for emergencies/break-glass, or must all outbound go through proxy only?
Logging: flow logs required by default? destination (CloudWatch vs S3) and retention expectations (90d vs 365d).
SIEM: preferred integration (S3 export, CloudWatch subscription filters to central account, or third-party forwarder).
KMS: customer-managed CMK required for log buckets and any EBS/encryption; cross-account KMS constraints?
Identity: SSO/SAML for console access later; for POC, who will assume installer execution role and what permission boundary is acceptable?
internal_notes: This one will surface all the 'alpha pain' areas: endpoints + DNS + egress proxy + log destinations. Keep scope tight: VPC module defaults + clearly documented overrides; do not promise full on-prem Terraform package. Recommend early installer preflight run to validate endpoint coverage before they burn cycles debugging image pulls. If they prohibit NAT entirely, ensure module example uses endpoints + proxy pattern and explicitly calls out limitations.
